summary: Facepalm: Scan for 2026-10-01 (facepalm). I ran out of search capacity early, so there are only two candidates. Both are in the date window, and each has two opened sources from different publishers, with quotes checked against the fetched text. 1) The White House AI accord that Trump posted on Sept 29 gives his title as "President of the Unites States." Sources: TechCrunch and KOMO (National News Desk). 2) Sen. Eric Schmitt accused Jack Smith of attending an Atlanta Hawks game at the Sept 29 Senate Judiciary hearing. Smith had been at an Iowa Hawkeyes game in Maryland. Sources: KCUR/St. Louis Public Radio and CBS News. Both candidates are Republican political stories. I rechecked several earlier set-asides; none had gained a second accepted source. Genius: Genius scan for 2026-10-01 (window Sept 24 to Oct 1). The top pick is SpaceX's Starship reaching orbit for the first time on Flight 14 (Sept 28, Starbase, TX). It is sourced from CBS News and TechCrunch, with Space.com as a third source. The alternates are 2026 MacArthur Fellows announced Sept 29 and are from states other than Texas, the state used on 9/30: Kaiyu Guan (IL; Chicago Sun-Times plus the AP list on WRAL), Ellora Derenoncourt (NJ; PBS/AP plus Princeton's announcement) and Marika Holland (CO; the AP list on WRAL plus UCAR's announcement). The search tool hit its usage limit early, so no further science/journal stories were checked. Pair published.
